title: Nurse Float Shift Risk Handoff
oneLiner: A field-ready handoff tool that helps charge nurses expose unsafe float coverage before the shift breaks.
targetUser: Charge nurses, float pool coordinators, unit managers, and hospital staffing leads handling mixed RN, LPN, CNA, sitter, and agency coverage.
keyUX: Build a shift risk map from patient acuity, floated staff familiarity, violence flags, med complexity, and missing support roles, then generate a pre-shift escalation note.
searchSignals: S8 Becker's 2026 nursing turnover and workplace violence context: https://www.beckershospitalreview.com/quality/nursing/the-current-state-of-nursing-2026/
S9 Reddit r/nursing operational cutbacks and support-role changes: https://www.reddit.com/r/nursing/comments/1tpmht0/what_subtle_changes_are_you_noticing_in_your/
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive web app prototype called "Nurse Float Shift Risk Handoff" for charge nurses, float pool coordinators, and unit managers. The app should help a charge nurse map patient acuity, floated staff familiarity, violence or sitter risk, missing support roles, med complexity, and break coverage before the shift starts, then generate a concise escalation note for the supervisor. Required sections: shift command header, patient acuity board, float staff familiarity matrix, missing support role flags, violence and sitter risk lane, break coverage timeline, escalation note composer, and post-shift incident recap. Use realistic hospital shift sample data while avoiding diagnosis or clinical decision support claims. Design direction: use the `field-ops` profile with durable shift-board styling, strong alert hierarchy, mobile-friendly controls, badge-like role markers, and a practical tone for frontline operators under pressure.
